title: Negotiating from Weakness
description: What to do when the other side holds most of the cards.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: When you have little leverage, the instinct is to bluff or to accept anything. The better path is to improve your alternatives, shrink the deal to what you can defend, and lean on time and information rather than force.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: Leverage comes from alternatives, information and patience — not only from size. Building even a modest alternative changes your behaviour, which the other side can read.

sections.title: Real-Life Examples
content: A small supplier winning better terms because it has a second buyer, however modest.
A candidate improving an offer because they have any other live option.

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: Improving your walk-away option before you negotiate.
Narrowing the deal to what genuinely matters.

sections.title: How to Use It
sections.content: Before you negotiate, build or strengthen your best alternative. Then trade on information and time, and keep the deal small and specific.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: Bluffing about alternatives you do not have.
Accepting terms you cannot actually live with.

sections.title: Defense Strategies
content: Never bluff a walk-away you would not take.
If you have no alternative, work on that first — not on the negotiation.

sections.title: Mistakes People Make
content: Trying to win the whole deal instead of the part that matters.

sections.title: Key Lessons
content: Leverage is built, not just held.
Keep the deal small when you are weak.
